newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares draw breath, insurers drag on market.
newsitem.headline: German shares draw breath, insurers drag on market.

text.p: German shares weakened in early trade on Tuesday, dragged lower by losses on heavyweight insurance shares, as the market drew breath after its sharp dollar-driven gains on Monday.
"It's time to take stock," said a Frankfurt dealer.
"If the market keeps going like a rocket, we could be heading for a somersault backward."
The IBIS DAX index, which tracks electronic trade in the top 30 German shares, was down 24.37 points at 4,117.82 points at 0708 GMT.
The dollar's drop from Monday's highs was the main trigger.
The U.S. currency, which had traded above or close to 1.79 marks throughout German share trade on Monday, was trading clearly below that level early on Tuesday.
Dollar stength invariably boosts the German share market, since top German industrial corporations are mainly strongly dependent on exports to the U.S.
Export-driven shares weakened on Tuesday, with carmaker Daimler-Benz AG, for example, down 1.10 marks at 147.80 marks.
Declines on shares in Allianz AG and Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG also weighed on the market.
Both shares had shot higher on Monday, with Munich Re rising nearly seven percent in bourse trade, after it reported higher than expected earnings for the 1996/1997 business year.
Munich Re was down 90 marks, or 1.4 percent, at 6,340 marks while Allianz was down 1.7 percent at 425.10 marks.
Despite the weak start, dealers said they did not expect any heavy selling pressure on the market, predicting that the DAX would trade in a range between 4,100 and 4,150 points.
"This is not a consolidation, it's a break," said one trader. "The money will keep coming in."
